title: India's First Human Metabolic Chamber Opens at CMC Vellore
excerpt: The room-sized calorimeter, built by TIFR and CMC Vellore, tracks how volunteers use energy over 24 hours or more, generating India-specific data on diabetes, obesity and metabolism.
body:
• Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava inaugurated India's first dedicated Human Metabolic Chamber Facility at Christian Medical College (CMC), Vellore, on Monday, November 23, 2026.
  • The room-sized calorimeter, set up jointly by the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR) and CMC Vellore, measures oxygen use and carbon dioxide production while a volunteer lives, eats and sleeps inside for 24 hours or longer.
  • The facility is meant to generate India-specific evidence on energy use, diabetes, obesity and metabolic disorders, rather than relying on data from other populations.
  • It was funded by the Department of Atomic Energy with CSR support from Hindustan Unilever, and technical advice from NUTRIM at Maastricht University.

India's first dedicated Human Metabolic Chamber Facility was inaugurated at Christian Medical College (CMC), Vellore, on Monday by Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava. Established jointly by the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR) and CMC Vellore, the facility will strengthen research into human metabolism, nutrition, diabetes, obesity and other metabolic conditions, the Press Information Bureau said in its official release.

What the chamber measures

The Human Metabolic Chamber is a room-sized calorimeter. It measures oxygen consumption and carbon dioxide production while a volunteer lives, eats and sleeps inside for 24 hours or longer. Those measurements show total energy expenditure and how the body uses fat and carbohydrates across meals, physical activity and sleep.

The facility complements the National Analytical Facility for Nutrition and Metabolism Research run by TIFR's Advanced Research Unit on Metabolism, Development & Aging (ARUMDA), established last year, so that molecular and biochemical measurements can be linked with the body's actual energy use. CMC Vellore brings clinical expertise in diabetes and endocrine and metabolic disorders, including its past studies on insulin sensitivity and energy expenditure in people with a history of undernutrition and low birth weight.

Why India-specific data

Inaugurating the facility, Srivastava called for robust, India-specific research to strengthen understanding of metabolic risks and inform preventive healthcare, noting that findings from other countries may not adequately capture the diversity and specific risk profiles of India's population. She congratulated TIFR, ARUMDA and CMC Vellore on the initiative and acknowledged the Department of Atomic Energy for supporting the collaboration.

She also pointed to the government's wider prevention push under Ayushman Bharat: 1.87 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs providing primary care and population-based screening for non-communicable diseases, over 781 district NCD clinics and 6,489 NCD clinics at community health centres, and more than 7.8 crore cumulative yoga sessions conducted at the Mandirs. She encouraged TIFR, ARUMDA and CMC Vellore to work with the Health Ministry and other national institutions, including the proposed Pan-AIIMS Research Consortium, on a focused research agenda.

Who built it

The facility was set up with funding from the Department of Atomic Energy and corporate social responsibility support from Hindustan Unilever Limited, with expert advice from NUTRIM at Maastricht University and network support from the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands in India. The inauguration was attended by CMC Vellore Director Prof. Biju George, TIFR Director Prof. Jayaram Chengalur and Prof. Felix Jebasingh of CMC Vellore's Department of Endocrinology, Diabetes and Metabolism, among others.
